Quick notes from Finance after a brief review — high level guidance and proposed PO controls.

1) Invoicing entity determines VAT treatment
   - If Redwood is invoiced by an EU-registered entity (Italy or Luxembourg) and the supply is B2B with Redwood as the customer (we provide a valid Redwood EU VAT/ID where required), the invoice should generally be processed under reverse-charge. Redwood will self-account where local rules require it.
   - If the supplier invoices us from a non-EU jurisdiction for services consumed outside the EU, VAT will typically not apply (treated as out-of-scope).

2) Marketplace / platform commissions nuance
   - For marketplace models we need the supplier to state whether the invoice is for a supply of services (platform fee) or a resale/third-party charge. That distinction affects whether the reverse-charge applies or whether the supplier should zero-rate as an export.

3) Required evidence (minimum)
   - Copy of supplier VAT certificate (attachment: FastPlatform_VAT_certificate.pdf) OR online VAT lookup URL for the invoicing entity.
   - Sample invoice showing the wording used and the legal invoice header. Prefer PDF. (attachment: sample_invoice_reverse_charge.pdf)
   - For Luxembourg invoicing entities, confirmation of local VAT registration (or note that they operate under an intra-group billing model).

4) PO tagging & AP processing (proposed controls)
   - Proposed PO fields: supplier_entity, supplier_vat_id, tax_tag (reverse_charge | zero_rate | out_of_scope), invoice_currency, pay_entity.
   - For your intake flow, Procurement should set tax_tag=reverse_charge if supplier_entity is EU and invoice shows reverse-charge wording. Finance will route to VAT-self-accounting workflow.
   - Where supplier invoices are split (platform fee vs vendor payout), we require separate line-item tagging on the PO and separate supporting invoices.

5) Examples of acceptable invoice line language (to include on supplier invoices):
   - \"Reverse charge — Article 44 and 196 of Directive 2006/112/EC applies; VAT to be self-accounted by the recipient.\"
   - Or: \"Export of services — no VAT charged under local rules\" (if supplier can show out-of-scope evidence).

Priyom: once procurement confirms which entity will issue the invoice to Redwood, set PO tax_tag accordingly. Laura: if there are any legal clauses we want in the Supplier Declaration (for marketplace commissions) flag them and I'll include in the intake checklist.

Ben

Hi Elena / FastPlatform AP team — thanks for the quick turnaround and for attaching the VAT cert. Based on Finance and Procurement input, here's the checklist we'll need to complete supplier onboarding and issue the first PO: 

1) Confirm invoicing entity (legal name + country) that will bill Redwood for platform fees. If multiple legal entities may invoice, list each with corresponding VAT ID.
2) Send a PDF sample invoice that includes: legal header, VAT number, invoice line(s) with reverse-charge wording (if applicable).
3) Upload official VAT certificate (we've received the 'FastPlatform_VAT_certificate.pdf' — thanks). If invoicing is by Luxembourg entity, please also confirm VAT registration details for that entity.
4) State whether the invoice lines split platform fee vs payout to third parties (if yes, provide separate invoices or clear line-item separation).

What Redwood will do once we have the documents:
- Procurement will create a PO with tax_tag set to either 'reverse_charge' or 'out_of_scope' depending on entity + invoice language. (PO will include field: non_us_supplier:reverse_charge=true if applicable.)
- Finance will route invoices that carry reverse-charge to our VAT self-accounting process. For zero-rated/out-of-scope invoices we'll process as standard AP.
